dialect: Sudanese Arabic as spoken in Khartoum
rules: Write the sound heard in the recording, not the spelling. Arabic script omits short vowels, so the transliteration cannot be worked out from the script by rule.
Long vowels are doubled: aa, ii, uu, ee, oo.
A doubled consonant (shadda) is written twice: kattar.
The article is written as heard and joined with a hyphen: al-beet, ash-shams.
Capital letters mark emphatic consonants and the deep h. Lower case is never emphatic, so a line never starts with a capital just because it is the start of a line.

letters.sound: hard g, as in galb (heart); write q only where q is actually sung
a stop made further back than English j

otherConsonants: All other consonants use their usual Latin letter.
